leaf.text: A large alternate leaf, 5 to 9 inches long and about as wide, with 3 to 5 lobes and coarse teeth. The veins spread from the leaf base like fingers.
leaf.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Platanus × hispanica (ID 307)

bark.text: Light brown bark that flakes off in patches and shows cream, olive and yellow patches below.
bark.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Platanus × hispanica (ID 307)

fruit.text: Round brown fruit balls, 1 to 1 1/2 inches across, usually two on one long thin stalk.
fruit.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Platanus × hispanica (ID 307)

leaf.text: An ovate to elliptic leaf, 2 to 5 1/2 inches long, with 3 to 5 pointed lobes that end in bristle tips. The upper side is shiny.

bark.text: Black bark with rough furrows between flat ridges.
bark.ref: FNA vol. 3, Quercus gravesii (efloras.org, taxon 233501040); Trees and Shrubs Online, Quercus gravesii

fruit.text: A small ovoid acorn, about 1/2 inch long, in a deep cup that covers a third to half of the nut.

leaf.text: A thick, shiny leaf with 3 to 5 rounded lobes. The middle lobes are often square and can make a cross shape. The underside is pale and soft.
leaf.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus margaretta (ID 427); FNA vol. 3, Quercus margaretta (efloras.org, taxon 233501059)

bark.text: Light gray to gray-brown scaly bark. Old bark has vertical ridges and is darker.
bark.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus margaretta (ID 427); FNA vol. 3, Quercus margaretta (efloras.org, taxon 233501059)

fruit.text: A light brown ovoid acorn, 1/2 to 1 inch long, in a bowl-shaped cup with thin scales that covers a third to half of the nut or more.
fruit.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus margaretta (ID 427); FNA vol. 3, Quercus margaretta (efloras.org, taxon 233501059)

leaf.text: An obovate leaf, 3 to 5 inches long, with 2 to 3 shallow, rounded or oblong lobes on each side. The lobes do not make a cross shape. The upper side is dark green and glossy, and the underside is grayish.

fruit.text: A light brown to dark reddish brown acorn, about 1/2 inch long, ovoid or oblong, in a shallow cup with flat gray scales. One to three acorns sit on the twig with almost no stalk.

leaf.text: An obovate leaf, 3 to 7 inches long and widest above the middle, with 6 to 8 shallow, rounded lobes on each side. The upper side is dark green and shiny, and the underside is pale gray.
leaf.ref: Trees and Shrubs Online, Quercus bicolor; Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus bicolor (ID 313)

bark.text: Gray scaly bark. Old bark has irregular fissures and flat ridges.
bark.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus bicolor (ID 313); FNA vol. 3, Quercus bicolor (efloras.org, taxon 233501012)

fruit.text: A tan acorn, about 1 inch long, one or two on a long thin stalk of 2 inches or more. The bowl-shaped cup covers about a third of the nut.
fruit.ref: Virginia Tech Dendrology fact sheet, Quercus bicolor (ID 313); FNA vol. 3, Quercus bicolor (efloras.org, taxon 233501012)
